topic.examWeightHint: Unit 1 is one two-hour calculator paper of 100 marks, sat every Summer. Optimisation is the last or second-last question and the best discriminator on the paper: 7 marks over three parts in Summer 2025 Q14, and multi-part questions of 8 to 12 marks in Summer 2018 Q12, Summer 2019 Q14, Summer 2022 Q13 and Summer 2024 Q13. The shape is fixed: one or two show-that parts worth 1 or 2 marks each that build the expression, then a 4 or 5 mark part reading using calculus, find the value of x ... showing that it is a maximum, and often a final 1 or 2 mark part asking for the optimised quantity itself. Schemes run M1 for the rewrite of a negative power, MW1 for the derivative, M1 and W1 for setting it to zero and solving, MW1 for the second derivative with its sign, and W1 for the quantity with its unit.

Rewrite a/x as ax⁻¹ before differentiating, and the index steps down to −2
After solving dy/dx = 0, take the square root where one is needed and reject the negative root
Show the second derivative and its sign: positive is a minimum, negative is a maximum
Finish by substituting back for the quantity the question named, with its unit

workedExamples.stem:
A rectangular flower bed is made against a straight wall. The other three sides are edged with $48$ m of timber. The two sides at right angles to the wall are each $x$ m long.
Find the value of $x$ that gives the greatest possible area, show that it is a maximum, and state that greatest area.

figure.src: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg viewBox='0 0 520 250' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' role='img' aria-label='A rectangular garden bed against a wall: the two sides at right angles to the wall are each x metres and the side facing the wall is y metres'><title>A rectangular garden bed against a wall: the two sides at right angles to the wall are each x metres and the side facing the wall is y metres</title><path d='M 124 70 L 406 70' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='4' fill='none' stroke-linecap='round'/><path d='M 140 70 L 140 190 L 390 190 L 390 70' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.08' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><text x='265' y='58' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>the wall costs nothing to fence</text><text x='265' y='212' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>y m, the side facing the wall</text><text x='130' y='130' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='end'>x m</text><text x='400' y='130' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='start'>x m</text><text x='260' y='240' font-family='inherit' font-size='11.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>48 m of timber covers those three sides only</text></svg>
figure.alt: A rectangular flower bed against a wall, with two sides of x metres, the side facing the wall y metres, and the 48 metres of timber covering those three sides

steps.working: The timber covers two sides of $x$ and one side of $y$, so $2x + y = 48$ and $y = 48 - 2x$.
steps.decision: The wall is the fourth side and costs nothing, which is the only reason this problem has an answer. Reading that from the picture is the first mark.

options: Because the wall replaces one of the four sides
Because the bed is a square
Because x and y are always equal
whyMenu.explain: Three sides are edged, not four, so the constraint is 2x + y rather than 2x + 2y.

steps.decision: Substituting the constraint leaves one letter, which is what differentiation needs. Expand it now: an unsimplified expression is where slips start.
Each term separately: multiply by the power, step the power down. The term in x contributes its coefficient, never nothing.

steps.working: Set the gradient to zero: $-4x + 48 = 0$, so $4x = 48$ and $x = 12$.
steps.decision: A largest or smallest value sits where the quantity stops changing, so the derivative is zero there.

steps.working: Differentiate again: $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -4$, which is negative, so $x = 12$ gives a maximum.
steps.decision: The question is not answered until the turning point has been named. A negative second derivative is the evidence the scheme pays for.
The question asked for the area, not for x. Finishing at $x = 12$ leaves the last marks on the table, and the unit belongs on the answer line.

options: Because the question asked for an area, not a length
Because x is always the answer
Because the units are the same either way
whyMenu.explain: x is a width in metres; the area is in square metres. Read the last line of the question before writing anything down.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: $x = 12$ m gives a maximum, because $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -4$, and the greatest area is $288$ m².

workedExamples.stem:
A rectangular vegetable plot of area $54$ m² is fenced round all four sides and has one more fence across it, parallel to the two shorter sides. The plot is $x$ m across.
Find the value of $x$ that uses the least fencing, show that it is a minimum, and state that least length.

figure.src: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg viewBox='0 0 520 260' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' role='img' aria-label='A rectangular vegetable plot x metres across and y metres deep, of area 54 square metres, with one extra fence of length y across the middle'><title>A rectangular vegetable plot x metres across and y metres deep, of area 54 square metres, with one extra fence of length y across the middle</title><rect x='110' y='60' width='300' height='150' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.07' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M 260 60 L 260 210' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2' fill='none' stroke-dasharray='6 4' stroke-linecap='round'/><text x='260' y='46' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>x m across</text><text x='100' y='135' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='end'>y m</text><text x='268' y='135' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='start'>the extra fence, y m</text><text x='260' y='234' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>area 54 m²</text></svg>
figure.alt: A rectangular vegetable plot of area 54 square metres, x metres across and y metres deep, with one extra fence of length y across the middle

steps.working: The area fixes the depth: $xy = 54$, so $y = \frac{54}{x}$.
steps.decision: Here the constraint is an area rather than a length, so the substitution produces a fraction instead of a subtraction.

steps.working: The fencing is two sides of $x$, two sides of $y$ and one more $y$ across the middle: $L = 2x + 3y = 2x + \frac{162}{x}$.
steps.decision: Count the fences on the picture one at a time. Leaving the middle fence out is the single commonest way this expression goes wrong.

options: Because the extra fence is a third side of length y
Because the extra fence is a third side of length x
Because the extra fence has no length
whyMenu.explain: The fence runs parallel to the shorter sides, so it is as long as they are, and the total in y becomes 3y rather than 2y.

steps.working: Write the fraction as a power and differentiate: $L = 2x + 162x^{-1}$, so $\frac{dL}{dx} = 2 - \frac{162}{x^{2}}$.
steps.decision: The power rule only speaks about powers, so the fraction has to come up as a negative index first. The index steps down from -1 to -2.

steps.working: Set it to zero: $\frac{162}{x^{2}} = 2$, so $x^{2} = 81$ and $x = 9$.
steps.decision: Take the square root, and take only the positive one: a length cannot be negative, so the other root is discarded with a word.

steps.working: Second derivative: $\frac{d^{2}L}{dx^{2}} = \frac{324}{x^{3}}$. At $x = 9$ that is $\frac{4}{9}$, which is positive, so this is a minimum.
steps.decision: This second derivative depends on x, so the value of x has to be put in before the sign can be read. A general statement is not evidence.
Check the answer against the picture: a plot 9 m by 6 m has an area of 54 m², so the constraint is satisfied and the arithmetic holds.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: $x = 9$ m gives a minimum, because $\frac{d^{2}L}{dx^{2}} = \frac{4}{9}$ there, and the least fencing is $36$ m.

workedExamples.stem:
A notice is printed on a rectangular card. The printed part has an area of $300$ cm² and is $w$ cm wide. There is a margin of $3$ cm at each side and $4$ cm at the top and at the bottom.
Show that the total area of the card is $A = 8w + 348 + \frac{1800}{w}$ cm², then find the least possible total area.

figure.src: data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg viewBox='0 0 520 300' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' role='img' aria-label='A notice: a printed rectangle of area 300 square centimetres with margins of 3 centimetres at each side and 4 centimetres at the top and bottom'><title>A notice: a printed rectangle of area 300 square centimetres with margins of 3 centimetres at each side and 4 centimetres at the top and bottom</title><rect x='116' y='18' width='278' height='224' fill='none' fill-opacity='0' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='150' y='60' width='210' height='140' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.09' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='255' y='130' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>printed area 300 cm²</text><text x='255' y='54' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>4 cm margin</text><text x='255' y='230' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>4 cm margin</text><text x='108' y='130' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='end'>3 cm</text><text x='402' y='130' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='start'>3 cm</text><text x='255' y='262' font-family='inherit' font-size='12.5' fill='currentColor' text-anchor='middle'>w is the width of the printed part only</text></svg>
figure.alt: A notice with a printed rectangle of area 300 square centimetres and margins of 3 centimetres at the sides and 4 centimetres at the top and bottom

steps.working: The printed part is $w$ by $h$ with $wh = 300$, so $h = \frac{300}{w}$.
steps.decision: The fixed printed area is the constraint. Naming the printed height h before using it keeps the two rectangles apart in your head.

steps.working: The card is wider by two side margins and taller by two end margins: $(w + 6)$ by $\left(h + 8\right)$.
steps.decision: Two margins, not one, on each measurement. Halving this is the slip that makes the whole answer plausible and wrong.
Every line of a show-that earns its own mark, so write the expansion before the tidy version. The printed result is the last line you write, never the first.
The constant 348 goes to zero and the fraction is differentiated as 1800w to the power -1, whose index steps down to -2.

steps.working: Set it to zero: $\frac{1800}{w^{2}} = 8$, so $w^{2} = 225$ and $w = 15$ cm.
steps.decision: Only the positive root is a width. Leaving the answer as w squared is the last place this question is commonly abandoned.

steps.working: Second derivative: $\frac{d^{2}A}{dw^{2}} = \frac{3600}{w^{3}}$, which at $w = 15$ is $\frac{16}{15}$: positive, so the area is least here.
steps.decision: Positive means the gradient is climbing through zero, which is a dip, and a dip in area is the smallest card.

steps.working: The least total area is $A = 348 + 8 \times 15 + \frac{1800}{15} = 588$ cm².
steps.decision: That is a card $21$ cm by $28$ cm, which multiplies back to $588$, so the answer checks against the picture.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: $w = 15$ cm gives a minimum, and the least total area of the card is $588$ cm².

twin.stem:
A workshop makes $x$ trays a week, and the cost of making each tray is $C = 2x + 15 + \frac{800}{x}$ pounds.
Find the number of trays a week that makes the cost of each tray least.

items.stem:
Three checks on what this lesson is built from. None of them is the new method, so answer from what you already know.
A rectangle $x$ m by $y$ m has area $54$ m². Write $y$ in terms of $x$.
items.skill: Rearrange a product to make one letter the subject

options.feedback: Dividing both sides of $xy = 54$ by $x$ leaves $y$ on its own. That fraction is what turns an optimisation problem into one letter.
Subtracting undoes an addition. Here $x$ and $y$ are multiplied, so the opposite operation is division.
That would make $y$ grow with $x$. A fixed area means the two measurements work against each other.
Multiply by the power $-1$ and step the index down to $-2$.
The coefficient is multiplied by the power, and that power is $-1$, so the sign changes.
The index steps down from $-1$, and down from $-1$ is $-2$.

items.stem: Solve $x^{2} = 81$ for the positive value of $x$.

options.feedback: Both roots are $9$ and $-9$; a length takes the positive one.
That is the value of $x^{2}$. The square root still has to be taken before you have $x$.
Halving undoes doubling, not squaring. The opposite of squaring is the square root.

items.stem: A bed against a wall uses $48$ m of edging on three sides, the two ends being $x$ m each. Which constraint is right?
items.skill: Read a constraint from a picture

options.feedback: Two ends and one front, because the wall takes the fourth side.
That fences all four sides and ignores the wall. It would give a greatest area of $144$ m² instead of $288$ m².
That is an area of 48 m², but 48 m of edging is a length. The constraint has to add up the sides.

items.stem: You have solved $\frac{dA}{dx} = 0$ and found a value of $x$. What does the scheme want next?
items.skill: Know the step after solving the derivative

options.text: The second derivative, with its value and sign
options.feedback: A stationary value is not yet a maximum. The second derivative is the evidence the mark is for.

options.text: Nothing more; the value of $x$ is the answer
options.feedback: The question asks for a maximum or a minimum, so the turning point has to be named before the answer is complete.

options.text: A table of values on either side
options.feedback: A sign check either side is valid mathematics, but where the stem says using calculus the second derivative is the expected evidence.

items.stem: The bed's area is $A = -2x^{2} + 48x$ and the greatest area is wanted. You have found $x = 12$. What do you write on the answer line?
items.skill: Answer the quantity the question asked for

options.feedback: Substituting $12$ back into $A$ gives $288$, and an area carries square metres.
That is the width that produces the greatest area, not the area itself. The last step is to substitute it back.
That is the other side of the bed. Both lengths are useful working, and neither is the area that was asked for.

items.stem: A quantity has $\frac{d^{2}P}{dx^{2}} = \frac{4}{9}$ at its stationary value. What has been shown?
items.skill: Read the sign of the second derivative

options.text: That the stationary value is a minimum
options.feedback: A positive second derivative means the gradient is climbing through zero, which is a dip.

options.text: That the stationary value is a maximum
options.feedback: The test runs the other way: positive names a minimum and negative names a maximum.

options.text: Nothing, because the value is a fraction
options.feedback: Only the sign matters, and a fraction has a sign like any other number. This one is positive.

items.skill: Differentiate a sum with a plain term in x and a negative power

options.feedback: The plain $x$ contributes $1$, and $576x^{-1}$ gives $-576x^{-2}$.
The fraction has been handled correctly and the plain $x$ has vanished. The derivative of $x$ is $1$, so that $1$ belongs in the answer.
The index is right. Multiplying $576$ by the power $-1$ makes that term negative.

context.setting: Differentiating an area expression that has already been formed

parts.stem:
The area of a flower bed is given by $A = -2x^{2} + 48x$, where $x$ is measured in metres.
Find $\frac{dA}{dx}$.
hints: Differentiate each term on its own.
The term $48x$ has power 1, so it leaves $48$ behind.
parts.workedSolution:
$-2x^{2}$ gives $-4x$, and $48x$ gives $48$.
So $\frac{dA}{dx} = -4x + 48$.

commonErrors.feedback: The squared term is right. The term $48x$ is a straight line of gradient $48$, so it leaves $48$ behind rather than nothing.
That is the value of $x$ you would get by going one step further and solving $-4x + 48 = 0$. This part asks only for the expression.

context.setting: Solving the derivative equal to zero

parts.stem:
A flower bed has $\frac{dA}{dx} = -4x + 48$.
Solve $\frac{dA}{dx} = 0$.
hints: Move the term in $x$ to the other side.
Then divide by its coefficient.
parts.workedSolution:
$-4x + 48 = 0$ gives $4x = 48$.
Dividing by $4$: $x = 12$.

context.setting: Differentiating a length expression with a negative power

parts.stem:
The fencing round a vegetable plot is given by $L = 2x + \frac{162}{x}$, where $x$ is measured in metres.
Find $\frac{dL}{dx}$.
hints: Rewrite the fraction with a negative index first.
Multiplying $162$ by the power $-1$ changes the sign.
The index steps down from $-1$ to $-2$.

commonErrors.feedback: The index has stepped down correctly. Multiplying $162$ by the power $-1$ makes that term negative, so it is subtracted.
The fraction is handled correctly and the term $2x$ has disappeared. Its derivative is the number $2$, which belongs in the answer.

context.setting: Solving a derivative with a negative power equal to zero

parts.stem:
A length is given by $L = 2x + \frac{162}{x}$ for $x > 0$, and $\frac{dL}{dx} = 2 - \frac{162}{x^{2}}$.
Solve $\frac{dL}{dx} = 0$.

scheme.for: $x = 9$, the negative root rejected because $x$ is a length

hints: Move the fraction to the other side.
Multiply both sides by $x^{2}$.
Take the square root, and keep the positive one.
parts.workedSolution:
$2 - \frac{162}{x^{2}} = 0$ gives $\frac{162}{x^{2}} = 2$.
Multiplying by $x^{2}$ and dividing by $2$: $x^{2} = 81$.
So $x = 9$, taking the positive root because $x$ is a length.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the value of $x^{2}$, reached correctly. One step is left: take the square root, which gives $x = 9$.

context.setting: A short maximum problem with the expression already formed

parts.stem:
A quantity is given by $A = x(20 - x)$ for $0 < x < 20$.
Using calculus, find the greatest value that $A$ can take.

scheme.for: setting the derivative to zero, giving $x = 10$

hints: Expand the bracket before differentiating.
Set the derivative to zero and solve.
The question asks for the value of $A$, so substitute back.
parts.workedSolution:
Expand: $A = -x^{2} + 20x$.
Differentiate: $\frac{dA}{dx} = -2x + 20$.
Set to zero: $x = 10$.
$\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -2$, which is negative, so this is a maximum.
Substitute back: $A = 10(20 - 10) = 100$.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the value of $x$ at the maximum, which is three of the four marks. The question asks for the greatest value of $A$, so put it back: $A = 100$.

methodLock.requiredMethod: Differentiate, set the derivative to zero and solve, then confirm the nature of the turning point with the second derivative.

context.setting: A short minimum problem with a negative power

parts.stem:
A cost is given by $C = 3x + \frac{300}{x}$ for $x > 0$.
Using calculus, find the value of $x$ which makes $C$ least.

scheme.for: setting it to zero and reaching $x^{2} = 100$
$\frac{d^{2}C}{dx^{2}} = \frac{600}{x^{3}}$, which is $\frac{3}{5}$ at $x = 10$, positive, so a minimum

hints: Rewrite the fraction as $300x^{-1}$.
Set the derivative to zero and multiply through by $x^{2}$.
Take the positive square root, then confirm with the second derivative.
parts.workedSolution:
$\frac{dC}{dx} = 3 - \frac{300}{x^{2}}$.
Set to zero: $\frac{300}{x^{2}} = 3$, so $x^{2} = 100$ and $x = 10$.
$\frac{d^{2}C}{dx^{2}} = \frac{600}{x^{3}}$, which at $x = 10$ is $\frac{3}{5}$: positive, so $C$ is least here.

commonErrors.feedback: That is $x^{2}$, so the method marks stand. Take the square root to reach $x = 10$.

parts.stem:
A cost is given by $C = 3x + \frac{300}{x}$, and it is least when $x = 10$.
Find that least cost.
hints: Put the value into the original expression, not into the derivative.
Work out both terms and add them.

commonErrors.feedback: That is what $\frac{dC}{dx}$ gives at $x = 10$, and it is zero there by definition. The cost itself comes from the original expression, where it is $60$.

context.setting: Naming a turning point from the second derivative

parts.stem:
A bed's area has $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -4$ at its stationary value.
Determine whether that value is a maximum or a minimum.

options.text: A maximum, because the second derivative is negative
options.feedback: A negative second derivative means the gradient is falling through zero, which is a peak.

options.text: A minimum, because the second derivative is negative
options.feedback: The value is read correctly and the conclusion is reversed. Negative names a maximum and positive names a minimum.

options.text: It cannot be decided without a sketch
options.feedback: The second derivative settles it on its own, which is exactly why the scheme asks for it.

scheme.for: $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -4$, which is negative, so the stationary value is a maximum

hints: Look only at the sign.
Negative names a maximum.
parts.workedSolution: $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -4$ is negative, so the gradient is falling through zero and the stationary value is a maximum.

parts.stem:
A rectangular vegetable plot is $x$ m across and $y$ m deep, and its area is $54$ m². It is fenced round all four sides, and one more fence runs across it parallel to the sides of length $y$.
Write down an expression in $x$ for the total length of fencing.
hints: Count the fences of each length separately.
The extra fence is parallel to the sides of length $y$, so it is $y$ long.

parts.workedSolution:
There are two sides of length $x$, two of length $y$, and one more of length $y$ across the middle, so $L = 2x + 3y$.
The area gives $y = \frac{54}{x}$.
So $L = 2x + 3 \times \frac{54}{x} = 2x + \frac{162}{x}$.

commonErrors.feedback: The substitution for $y$ is right, so the method mark stands. Only four fences have been counted: the extra one across the middle is another $y$, which makes the total $2x + 3y$.

parts.stem:
A workshop makes $x$ trays a week, and the cost of making each tray is $C = 2x + 15 + \frac{800}{x}$ pounds.
Using calculus, find the number of trays a week that makes the cost of each tray least.

$\frac{d^{2}C}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1600}{x^{3}}$, which at $x = 20$ is $\frac{1}{5}$: positive, so the cost is least at $20$ trays a week.

commonErrors.feedback: That is $x^{2}$, reached correctly. The square root is still to be taken, which gives $20$ trays.

parts.stem:
A notice is printed on a rectangular card. The printed part is $w$ cm wide, $h$ cm tall and has an area of $300$ cm². There is a margin of $3$ cm at each side and $4$ cm at the top and at the bottom.
Show that $h = \frac{300}{w}$.

accepted: The printed area is wh = 300, so dividing both sides by w gives h = 300/w

scheme.examinerNote: The area equation must appear; the printed result alone is not a derivation.

hints: Write down the area of the printed rectangle.
Then make $h$ the subject.
parts.workedSolution:
The printed rectangle is $w$ by $h$, so its area is $wh = 300$.
Dividing both sides by $w$ gives $h = \frac{300}{w}$.

parts.stem: Show that the total area of the card is $A = 8w + 348 + \frac{1800}{w}$ cm².

accepted: The card is (w + 6) by (h + 8), so A = wh + 8w + 6h + 48, and with h = 300/w that is 8w + 348 + 1800/w

scheme.examinerNote: Every line is wanted; the printed result cannot be the starting point.

hints: Each measurement grows by two margins.
Multiply the two brackets out before substituting.
Collect the two constant terms.
parts.workedSolution:
The card is $(w + 6)$ cm by $\left(h + 8\right)$ cm, so $A = (w + 6)(h + 8)$.
Multiplying out: $A = wh + 8w + 6h + 48$.
Substituting $wh = 300$ and $h = 300/w$ gives $A = 300 + 8w + 6(300/w) + 48 = 8w + 348 + \frac{1800}{w}$.

commonErrors.feedback: The printed expression has been copied down with nothing in front of it. A show-that pays for the derivation, so write the two brackets, the expansion and the substitution as three separate lines.

parts.stem: Using calculus, find the value of $w$ that makes the total area least, showing clearly that it is a minimum.

scheme.for: $w = 15$, the negative root rejected because $w$ is a width
$\frac{d^{2}A}{dw^{2}} = \frac{3600}{w^{3}}$, which is $\frac{16}{15}$ at $w = 15$, positive, so a minimum

hints: Write $\frac{1800}{w}$ as $1800w^{-1}$ before differentiating.
The constant term differentiates to zero.
After solving, differentiate a second time and substitute your value of $w$.
parts.workedSolution:
$\frac{dA}{dw} = 8 - \frac{1800}{w^{2}}$.
Set it to zero: $\frac{1800}{w^{2}} = 8$, so $w^{2} = 225$ and $w = 15$ cm, taking the positive root because $w$ is a width.
$\frac{d^{2}A}{dw^{2}} = \frac{3600}{w^{3}}$, which at $w = 15$ is $\frac{16}{15}$.
That is positive, so the total area is least when $w = 15$ cm.

commonErrors.feedback: That is $w^{2}$, which is three of the five marks. Take the square root for $w = 15$, then show the second derivative is positive.

parts.stem: Find the least possible total area of the card.
hints: Substitute your value of $w$ into the expression from part (b).
A check: the card is $21$ cm by $28$ cm.
parts.workedSolution:
$A = 348 + 8 \times 15 + \frac{1800}{15} = 348 + 120 + 120 = 588$ cm².
As a check, the card is $21$ cm by $28$ cm, and $21 \times 28 = 588$.

commonErrors.feedback: The number is right and the substitution earns its mark. The quantity is an area, so the answer line needs its unit: $588$ cm².
That is the printed width in centimetres, which part (c) already asked for. This part wants the area of the whole card, which is $588$ cm².

parts.stem:
Two rectangular pens are built side by side against a long barn wall. Altogether they use $36$ m of fencing for the two ends, the far side and the divider between them. Each end, and the divider, is $x$ m long, and the far side is $y$ m long.
Show that $y = 36 - 3x$.

accepted: The fencing covers two ends, the divider and the far side, so 3x + y = 36, giving y = 36 - 3x

scheme.for: $3x + y = 36$ read from the arrangement, then rearranged
scheme.examinerNote: The three lengths of x must be counted: two ends and the divider.

hints: How many fences are $x$ metres long?
The wall is not fenced.
parts.workedSolution:
Three fences are $x$ m long: the two ends and the divider. One fence is $y$ m long: the far side.
So $3x + y = 36$, and rearranging gives $y = 36 - 3x$.

parts.stem: Show that the total area enclosed is $A = -3x^{2} + 36x$ m².

accepted: The area is xy, and substituting y gives x(36 - 3x) = 36x - 3x^2

hints: The two pens together form one rectangle.
Substitute the expression for $y$ from part (a).
parts.workedSolution:
The two pens together are one rectangle $x$ m by $y$ m, so $A = xy$.
Substituting from part (a): $A = x(36 - 3x) = -3x^{2} + 36x$.

parts.stem: Using calculus, find the value of $x$ which gives the greatest total area, showing clearly that it is a maximum.

scheme.for: $\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -6$, which is negative, so a maximum

hints: Differentiate the expression from part (b).
Set it to zero and solve.
Differentiate again and read the sign.
parts.workedSolution:
$\frac{dA}{dx} = -6x + 36$.
Set it to zero: $6x = 36$, so $x = 6$.
$\frac{d^{2}A}{dx^{2}} = -6$, which is negative, so $x = 6$ gives the greatest area.

parts.stem: Find the greatest total area enclosed.
hints: Substitute your value of $x$ into the area.
A check: $y = 18$ m, and $6 \times 18$ is the same number.
parts.workedSolution:
$A = 36 \times 6 - 3 \times 6^{2} = 108$ m².
As a check, $y = 36 - 3 \times 6 = 18$ m, and $6 \times 18 = 108$.

commonErrors.feedback: The number is right and the substitution earns its mark. The quantity is an area, so the answer line needs its unit: $108$ m².
That is the value of $x$ from part (c), a length in metres. The area is $108$ m².

parts.stem:

$C = 2x + 15 + \frac{800}{x}$

hints: Rewrite the fraction with a negative index.
The constant $15$ differentiates to zero.

commonErrors.feedback: The index is right. Multiplying $800$ by the power $-1$ makes that term negative, so it is subtracted rather than added.
The fraction is handled correctly and the term $2x$ has gone. Its derivative is the number $2$, which belongs in the answer.

parts.stem: Using calculus, find the number of trays a week that makes the cost of each tray least.

scheme.for: $x = 20$, the negative root rejected because $x$ is a number of trays

hints: Set the derivative from part (a) to zero.
Multiply both sides by $x^{2}$.
Take the positive square root.
parts.workedSolution:
Set $\frac{dC}{dx} = 0$: $\frac{800}{x^{2}} = 2$.
Multiplying by $x^{2}$ and dividing by $2$: $x^{2} = 400$.
So $x = 20$ trays a week, taking the positive root.

commonErrors.feedback: That is $x^{2}$, so two of the three marks stand. One step is left: take the square root for $20$ trays.

parts.stem: Show clearly that this number of trays gives the least cost.

accepted: d2C/dx2 = 1600x^-3, and at x = 20 that is 1/5, which is positive, so the cost is a minimum
The second derivative is 1600/x^3, which at x = 20 is 1/5, a positive value, so this is a minimum

scheme.for: the value $\frac{1}{5}$ at $x = 20$, positive, so a minimum
scheme.examinerNote: A word with no number attached earns nothing here.

hints: Differentiate the derivative.
Substitute your value of $x$.
Say what the sign of that number means.

Differentiating again: $\frac{d^{2}C}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1600}{x^{3}}$, that is $1600/x^3$.
At $x = 20$ this is $\frac{1}{5}$, which is positive.
A positive second derivative means the gradient is climbing through zero, so the cost is at a minimum.

parts.stem:
A rectangular field of area $288$ m² lies beside a straight river. The side along the river needs no fence. The side opposite the river is $x$ m long and the two ends are each $y$ m long.
Show that $y = \frac{288}{x}$.

accepted: The area is xy = 288, so dividing by x gives y = 288/x

hints: Write down the area of the rectangle.
Make $y$ the subject.
parts.workedSolution:
The field is $x$ m by $y$ m, so $xy = 288$.
Dividing both sides by $x$ gives $y = \frac{288}{x}$.

parts.stem: Show that the total length of fencing is $L = x + \frac{576}{x}$ m.

accepted: The fence covers the far side and the two ends, so L = x + 2y = x + 2(288/x) = x + 576/x

hints: Three sides are fenced, not four.
Two of them are the ends, each $y$ m.
Now replace $y$.
parts.workedSolution:
The fence runs along the side opposite the river and the two ends, so $L = x + 2y$.
Substituting $y = 288/x$ gives $L = x + 2(288/x) = x + \frac{576}{x}$.

commonErrors.feedback: That fences all four sides. The river takes the side opposite $x$, so only one length of $x$ and the two ends are paid for.

parts.stem: Using calculus, find the value of $x$ which uses the least fencing, showing clearly that it is a minimum.

scheme.for: $\frac{dL}{dx} = 1 - \frac{576}{x^{2}}$, including the $1$ from the term in $x$
$x = 24$, the negative root rejected because $x$ is a length
$\frac{d^{2}L}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1152}{x^{3}}$, which is $\frac{1}{12}$ at $x = 24$, positive, so a minimum

hints: The plain $x$ differentiates to $1$, not to nothing.
Multiply through by $x^{2}$ after setting the derivative to zero.
Confirm with the second derivative at your value of $x$.
parts.workedSolution:
Rewrite: $L = x + 576x^{-1}$, so $\frac{dL}{dx} = 1 - \frac{576}{x^{2}}$.
Set it to zero: $\frac{576}{x^{2}} = 1$, so $x^{2} = 576$ and $x = 24$ m, taking the positive root.
$\frac{d^{2}L}{dx^{2}} = \frac{1152}{x^{3}}$, which at $x = 24$ is $\frac{1}{12}$: positive, so this is the least fencing.

commonErrors.feedback: That is $x^{2}$, so three of the five marks stand. Taking the square root gives $x = 24$ m.

parts.stem: Find the least length of fencing needed.
hints: Substitute $x = 24$ into $L$.
A check: $y = 12$ m, so the three sides are 24, 12 and 12.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the value of $x$ from part (c), the length of one side. The fencing is all three sides together, which is $48$ m.

findTheMistake.stem: Ruairí was asked for the least length of fencing for a field of area $288$ m² beside a river, where $L = x + \frac{576}{x}$. His working:
studentWorking: The least length of fencing is 24 m
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong:
Lines 1 to 4 are all correct, and they are worth most of the marks.
Line 5 reports the value of $x$, which is the length of one side of the field. The question asked for the total fencing, and that is $L$.
Substituting back gives $L = 24 + \frac{576}{24} = 48$ m.
correction: The least length of fencing is 48 m
findTheMistake.feedback: The calculus is sound and it earns its marks. What is missing is the last line: a value of $x$ is not the quantity the question named. Read the final sentence of the question again, substitute, and write the answer with its unit. Here the fencing is $48$ m, made up of $24$ m along the far side and $12$ m at each end.

findTheMistake.stem: Méabh was asked to show that the stationary value of $A = -3x^{2} + 36x$ is a maximum. Her working:
studentWorking: -6 is negative so this is a minimum
The area is least when x = 6
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong:
Lines 1 to 3 are exactly right, including the second derivative, which is the step most candidates forget altogether.
Line 4 reads the sign the wrong way round. A negative second derivative means the gradient is falling as it passes through zero: up, level, down, which is a peak.
Positive names a minimum; negative names a maximum.
correction: -6 is negative so this is a maximum
The area is greatest when x = 6
findTheMistake.feedback: All the calculus is right, so the method and working marks up to line 3 stand. Only the reading of the sign has slipped. Picture the gradient itself: if it is decreasing as it crosses zero, the curve rose to the point and then fell, and that is a maximum. A quick sanity check also helps here, since a fixed length of fencing can enclose a largest area but has no smallest one.

findTheMistake.stem: Cara was asked for the greatest area of a bed built against a wall with $48$ m of edging on three sides, the two ends each $x$ m. Her working:
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong:
Everything from line 2 onwards is correct working on the expression in line 1, which is why the error is so hard to spot on the page.
Line 1 fences all four sides. The wall provides one of them, so the edging covers two ends of $x$ and one side of $y$ only: $2x + y = 48$.
That gives $y = 48 - 2x$ and $A = -2x^{2} + 48x$, whose greatest value is $288$ m², not $144$ m².
findTheMistake.feedback: The calculus is faultless, and that is the part worth rehearsing. The first mark is the one lost outright, and it takes the accuracy marks with it, because every later line is correct working on an expression that was never the right one. Before writing a constraint, count on the diagram which sides actually carry fencing: here the wall takes one side, so only three lengths are paid for, and the answer roughly doubles to $288$ m².

prompts.prompt: What are the five steps of an optimisation question?
prompts.answer: Read the constraint, use it to write the quantity in one letter, differentiate and set the derivative to zero, confirm the nature with the second derivative, then substitute back for the quantity asked.

prompts.prompt: What does the word constraint mean in one of these questions?
prompts.answer: The sentence or diagram that ties the two letters together, such as a fixed length of fencing or a fixed area.

prompts.prompt: A bed is fenced on three sides against a wall, with ends of $x$ and a front of $y$. Why is the constraint not $2x + 2y$?
prompts.answer: The wall provides the fourth side, so only two ends and one front are fenced.

prompts.prompt: How do you differentiate a term such as $\frac{162}{x}$?
prompts.answer: Rewrite it as $162x^{-1}$, multiply by the power $-1$ and step the index down to $-2$, giving $-162x^{-2}$.

prompts.prompt: After solving $\frac{dA}{dx} = 0$, what does the scheme still want?
prompts.answer: The second derivative, worked out at that value of x, with its sign read as a maximum or a minimum.

prompts.prompt: You reach $x^{2} = 81$. What is left to do?
prompts.answer: Take the square root, giving $x = 9$, and reject the negative root because a length cannot be negative.

prompts.prompt: You have found the value of $x$ that maximises an area. Are you finished?
prompts.answer: Only if the question asked for x; otherwise substitute it back to find the area, the length or the cost that was asked for, with its unit.

prompts.prompt: What do the words using calculus in a stem forbid?
prompts.answer: Any non-calculus route: a table of values, a graph read by eye or a calculator maximum earns nothing.

prompts.prompt: Which optimisation contexts are not asked on this specification?
prompts.answer: Three-dimensional problems such as boxes, and anything involving pi.

findings.asked: Show an expression, then optimise it in context.
findings.wentWrong: In the 'show' part terms were added but not expanded step by step; few progressed in the calculus; some computed a different quantity (total shoppers) at the end.
findings.rule: Show every line of a 'show that'; finish with the quantity asked.

findings.asked: Area and perimeter expressions, a constraint, then the maximum area.
findings.wentWrong: Expressions were left unsimplified, causing later slips; many did not realise calculus was needed for the last part; some forgot to show the value was a maximum.
findings.rule: Simplify each expression, differentiate, and confirm max/min with the second derivative.

findings.asked: Form L from a diagram, then minimise it.
findings.wentWrong: Many could not read L = x + 2y from the diagram; when differentiating, the x term's derivative (1) was omitted, giving x squared = 900 and x = 30; the answer 30 mm was given instead of the required L = 60 mm.
findings.rule: Differentiate every term (x gives 1) and substitute back to find the quantity asked.

findings.wentWrong: Weaker candidates could not prove the two given results or apply them; most could differentiate the given expression.
findings.rule: Even if the setup is lost, differentiate the printed expression for method marks.

findings.asked: Form expressions, then find and classify a stationary point.
findings.wentWrong: Parts (i) and (ii) were strong. In (iii) the negative power of x was mishandled in the derivative and the resulting equation with fractional or negative exponents was hard to solve; the second derivative test was mostly done.
findings.rule: Differentiate negative powers carefully and solve for x before classifying.

insight.ruleToRemember: Build the expression from the constraint and simplify it; differentiate every term; set the derivative to zero and solve; use the second derivative to state max or min; then evaluate the quantity actually asked for.
insight.aStarSignal: Reading the constraint from a diagram, handling a negative power in the derivative, and finishing with the optimised quantity rather than x.
